evidence.reason: The finding is a design/optimization proposal, not an implementation error in existing intended behavior. The current code at line 192 uses `publisher.fetch()`, not the `GitLedger.fetch()` the finding names, so it is written against a different revision. More importantly, the fetch-under-lock is the documented, intended design: the adjacent comment (lines 191-192) explains a fresh fetch is needed because "New publication may remove eligibility without moving the job's T," and the contract's CRQ scheduling section describes due entries taking the shared lock (non-blocking) with only *coverage* explicitly kept off-lock (which the code honors at lines 203-205 via off-lock snapshots). Moving the fetch off-lock would change intended behavior and lock semantics, not fix a code defect. The specific "up to 300 seconds" latency and the claim that it delays other tick work are unproven allegations with no supplied evidence. Per the rules, an opportunity to harden/re-optimize an accepted mechanism does not itself establish a defect, and no contract clause requires an off-lock fetch.
